note: The backhand volley (jRkQB25IGPw, The Padel School, seen from the net): the racket read by eye off sheets of body-centred tiles (window.__sheet: 131.6 px to the metre, y down, each key in its own tile's pixels: only B to C counts): B the hand on the handle, C the face's centre, w the head's apparent width over its real one; the eighth number says which face the camera sees (-1 the back of the hand's from the take-back on; +1 while he stands side-on in the ready position, his free side to the camera). The parts where the body moves (the tracker's own points; the rest is drawing over frozen frames): 62.56-65.20 (the take-back), 73.20-74.64, 84.56-85.20 (the punch), 93.20-94.44 (the follow-through), a 100 fps camera at 25, no frame repeated; one frame is missing after the frozen contact frame (the wrist's step doubles there: `gap: 1`). Contact the ball on the strings at 85.20. Keys either side of a frozen frame are 0.01 s apart in the stroke: only one of each such pair is kept where the two readings differ (a 15 degree difference there is 1500 degrees a second to the spline, and it swung the racket round a loop before it).
